from solution import is_samepatterns


def test_issue_given_example():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' on the documented example."""
    # hand-computed: a->red, b->green consistent over 3 positions, so True
    assert is_samepatterns(["red", "green", "green"], ["a", "b", "b"]) == True


def test_issue_single_pair_matches():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' for one matching pair."""
    # hand-computed: single mapping a->red with 1 position, so True
    assert is_samepatterns(["red"], ["a"]) == True


def test_issue_mismatched_lengths():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' fails when lengths differ."""
    # hand-computed: 2 colors vs 3 patterns (2 != 3), cannot follow, so False
    assert is_samepatterns(["red", "green"], ["a", "b", "b"]) == False


def test_issue_same_pattern_requires_same_color():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' when same pattern maps to different colors."""
    # hand-computed: a->red then a->blue conflict over 2 positions, so False
    assert is_samepatterns(["red", "blue"], ["a", "a"]) == False


def test_issue_distinct_patterns_require_distinct_colors():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' when distinct patterns map to one color."""
    # hand-computed: a->red then b->red conflict (b should differ from a), so False
    assert is_samepatterns(["red", "red"], ["a", "b"]) == False


def test_issue_extended_consistent_mapping():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' for a longer consistent mapping."""
    # hand-computed: a->red (positions 0,3), b->green (positions 1,2) consistent over 4, so True
    assert is_samepatterns(["red", "green", "green", "red"], ["a", "b", "b", "a"]) == True


def test_issue_broken_mapping_at_end():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' when the last entry breaks the mapping."""
    # hand-computed: a->red at 0 but a->blue at 3 conflict over 4 positions, so False
    assert is_samepatterns(["red", "green", "green", "blue"], ["a", "b", "b", "a"]) == False


def test_issue_both_empty():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' for empty inputs."""
    # hand-computed: 0 colors vs 0 patterns (0 == 0) vacuously consistent, so True
    assert is_samepatterns([], []) == True


def test_issue_all_same_entries():
    """Check 'follows the sequence given in the patterns array' for all-identical entries."""
    # hand-computed: z->blue consistent over 3 positions, so True
    assert is_samepatterns(["blue", "blue", "blue"], ["z", "z", "z"]) == True


def test_contract_returns_exact_bool_on_match():
    """Check documented check returns a bool True value on a matching sequence."""
    # hand-computed: a->red, b->green consistent, expected literal True identity
    assert is_samepatterns(["red", "green", "green"], ["a", "b", "b"]) is True


def test_contract_returns_exact_bool_on_mismatch():
    """Check documented check returns a bool False value on a mismatched sequence."""
    # hand-computed: a->red then a->blue conflict, expected literal False identity
    assert is_samepatterns(["red", "blue"], ["a", "a"]) is False
